title: Accounts Payable Specialist
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
As an Accounts Payable Specialist, you will be responsible for performing accounts payable activities, including but not limited to, processing vendor invoices (Purchase Order based) as well as Landowner payments, ensuring the accuracy, timeliness, and integrity of financial data.  This role is also responsible for communicating with vendors regarding account discrepancies and supporting the Accounting functions. This position is based out of our downtown Chicago, IL office and will report to the Accounts Payable Manager.
Responsibilities
Process supplier payments in accordance with the terms of contracts
Respond to internal and external payment inquiries
Research and clear any discrepancies by working with other business units
Collaborate with internal and external business partners to expedite the resolution of issues pertaining to payments

5+ years of experience in a manufacturing or production environment.

Analytical Skills - The ability to review quantitative or conceptual problems and situations to draw appropriate and valid conclusions from data presented. This includes analyzing data to determine the most significant elements, identify common elements and themes in situations and actions, and recognize cause and effect relationships.
Compliance Management - The ability to supervise and observe the organization's conformity to various standards, procedures, rules, and regulations.
Project Quality Assurance - Knowledge of and the ability to apply systematic and continuing processes of making sure that the project is meeting specified requirements.
Quality Assurance - Knowledge of and the ability to follow systematic and continuing processes of checking to see whether a product, service, or process is meeting specified requirements. This includes knowledge of quality measurements and defined standards.
Regulatory Compliance - Knowledge of the rules, regulations, sanctions and other statutory requirements, guidelines and instructions relating to local and/or international governing bodies and organizations, both internally and externally.
Risk Analysis - Knowledge of Risk Management and Analysis, the process of measuring, or assessing risk and then developing strategies to manage the risk. This may include the ability to identify or develop strategies to transfer the risk to another party, avoid the risk, reduce the negative effect of the risk, and accept some or all of the consequences of a particular risk.
Construction Planning and Logistics
Construction - Knowledge of materials, methods, and the tools involved in the construction, repair, and engineering of buildings, houses, or other structures such as highways, roads, and bridges.
Construction Consulting - The ability to provide management, risk-based advisory, dispute resolution and strategic communications services across all construction and engineering.
Construction Management - Knowledge of specialized, project management techniques to oversee the planning, design, and construction of a project, from its beginning to its end.
Construction Planning - The ability to plan how the team will manage and execute a construction project.
Construction Processes - Knowledge of the design process (creating the description of a new facility, usually represented by detailed plans and specifications) and the construction planning process (identifying activities and resources required to make the design a physical reality).
Scope Management - The ability to manage scope over the course of a project, including determining which changes are essential, estimating their impact on the project, ensuring that changes do not expand scope beyond acceptable levels, and keeping a change record to track progress.
Financial Responsibility
Budgeting - Knowledge of and the ability to develop and utilize budgeting guidelines, practices, and techniques, including forecasting. This may include the knowledge of the department's procedures and reporting systems to establish financial budget information at an appropriate organizational level.
Construction Budgets - The ability to manage allotted funds for a specific building or remodeling project. The ability to anticipate all costs and expenses of the building process tracked through a form, tool, or spreadsheet.
Construction Risk - The ability to identify and manage any exposure to possible loss.
Cost Benefit - The ability to apply a systematic approach to estimating the strengths and weaknesses of alternatives (for example in transactions, activities, functional business requirements or projects investments) to determine options that provide the best approach to achieve benefits while preserving savings.
Financial Analysis - Knowledge of and the ability to use basic financial analysis (e.g., return on investment, value chain analysis) related to marketing effectiveness, resource allocations, and new business opportunities.
Project Cost - Knowledge of the process of identifying project resources, estimating costs, developing the budget, and managing the finances for a project.
Managing Vendor and Stakeholder Relationships
Conflict Resolution
The ability to manage conflict, disharmony, and strife among people and situations, while recognizing and addressing sensitivities.
Incident Handling - The ability to lead and direct others in the process of resolving escalated problems through communication.
Influence Others - The ability to garner support for initiatives by gaining the respect of others and inspiring trust and confidence.
Negotiation - The ability to achieve mutually satisfying agreements in negotiations with others by listening to their objectives, acting as the company's representative to effectively communicate the company's objective, and seeking common ground and collaborative solutions.
Team Facilitation - The ability to lead and orchestrate cross-functional teams to complete objectives. This includes the skills of communicating and collaborating with others, leveraging resources and tools, and coordinating processes.
Vendor Management - Knowledge of the process through which products and services are purchased for use by the corporation and the ability to identify, select, and manage vendors and suppliers who provide products and services to the company. This includes knowledge of the development of RFI's and RFP's and the ability to incorporate necessary technical requirements into contracts.
Project Management and Judgement
Change Management - The ability to define and implement procedures and/or technologies to deal with changes in the environment. This may include adapting to change, controlling change, and/or affecting change.
Decision Making - The ability to make decisions in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment. This includes the ability to define, diagnose, and determine an appropriate resolution, recommendation, or decision while considering alternatives and factors (e.g., resources, costs, tradeoffs).
Incident Management - The ability to identify, record, classify and apply a structured response process to manage incidents until the affected service is restored. Includes knowledge of the progression of an incident through occurrence of the incident, detection of the incident, diagnosis of the cause of failure, repair of the problem, recovery of the problem back to the live infrastructure and restoration of the service.
Multitasking - The ability to process and attend to multiple types of information and/or perform multiple tasks simultaneously.
Problem Solving - The ability to identify problems and review related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.
Project Management - Knowledge of and the ability to carry out the process of planning, organizing, and managing tasks and resources to accomplish a well-defined objective. This includes the ability to manage and provide project deliverables, optimize the contribution of the people involved, and assess the impact of project decisions on quality, productivity, schedules, cost, performance, etc.
Project Planning - The ability to manage a project schedule, defining and sequencing activities, estimating activity durations, and developing and controlling the schedule.
Vendor Selection and Evaluation - The ability to evaluate and select vendors who meet specifications and requirements. This includes knowledge of the development of RFI's and RFP's and the ability to incorporate necessary technical requirements into contracts.
Other:
Creativity - The ability to apply ingenuity, inventiveness, and imagination to the inclusive design and construction of a product, service, program, or initiative.
Oral Communication - The ability to make a verbal message understood and to receive/understand messages during in-person or remote (e.g., telephone) interactions.
Presentation Skills - The ability to prepare effective presentations in content and function, and to speak competently to the level of the audience.
Responsibilities
Budget and Controls - Develops and reports on scope, schedule, and budget of project. Implements project controls in work activities (e.g., project expenditure requests (PERs), Professional Service Requests (PSRs), change orders, and pay applications). Reduces cycle time, improves quality, and identifies and implements ways to lower cost.
Change Management  - Analyzes the industry for best practices and internal process flows to recommend changes resulting in cost savings, enhanced customer service, or improved asset management.
Coordination  - Acts as the primary point of contact for project development and delivery. Shapes and implements regional construction execution plans. Initializes and identifies opportunities to discuss and integrate lessons learned, advocating for safe and secure security-first mindset during project planning. Participates in and may drive Microsoft partner engagement, communications plans, and community events.
Drives Results - Makes decisions and influences partners to facilitate and accomplish complex issues impacting global construction projects (e.g., establishing and executing upon team goals, following business processes, engaging vendor relationships, and fostering cross-group collaboration efforts with the agreed-upon project strategy, milestone delivery, and core values and priorities (Safety, Security, Quality, Schedule, Cost)).
Financial Acumen - Creates, applies, and shares best practices to identify and drive cost-effective solutions for the strategic and tactical delivery of a construction project. Applies influence, strategy, and decision-making to drive solutions, schedules, and manage change with clients, sponsors, vendors, and operational units including lower-level staff and internal partners.
Goal Alignment  - Develops and maintains productive relationships with implementation partners, Operations, Security, Authorities having jurisdiction, and regional corporate leadership. Engages and sources other internal teams (e.g., Security [OSSC], Information Technology [MSIT], Legal, Project Engineering, Business Risk Management, etc.) to maintain the corporate vision and create goals for the project. Advises and directs internal teams and supporting specialty consultants to update and edit the Basis of Design (BOD) as needed.
Managing Resources  - Manages any alterations made to the project scope and adjusts the overall plan to accommodate these changes.

Develops/establishes program/project goals for teams, assigns overall responsibilities, ensures performance measurements, and seeks and delivers feedback to achieve timely results that prioritize security in documentation, design, and/or execution.
Project Tracking -  Reviews cost and key performance indicator (KPI) metrics, invoices, processes, and policies in order to communicate status to internal and external client partners. Takes accountability for on-schedule delivery by providing project progress reports including scope, schedule, and budget.
Risk Mitigation  - Establishes and communicates risk mitigation goals and develops metrics, dashboards and/or scorecards to drive progress. Presents and reports safety and security goals and progress to regional executive leadership.
Safety and Regulation  - Interprets safety standards and regulatory requirements (e.g., Americans with Disabilities Act [ADA]) to direct and enforce compliance and aggressive management of risk. Creates and reinforces safety program routines, security, project, and contractor audits. Demands safe environments/work sites and participates in governance, policies, and decision-making regarding risk compliance and management.
Technical Acumen  - Provides guidance and corrective action when necessary. Provides unique knowledge and answers questions regarding delivery options.

Establishes and monitors vendors' performance goals in order to ensure compliance with security policies, non-disclosure agreements, contracts, and prior audit results. MCAPS-Core accelerates customer outcomes and business growth. By uniting product, engineering, marketing, sales, customer success, and partners around a common customer mission, we help customers realize value faster and turn innovation into measurable business impact. Through deep technical expertise and differentiated go-to-market execution, we win competitively, capture market share, and scale repeatable growth motions. Within MCAPS - Core, the Customer Service & Support (CSS) organization builds trust and confidence for every person and organization through delivering a seamless support experience. This Technical Program Manager/Sr Technical Program Manager role, housed within the Worldwide MCAPs Team, works to develop strong ties with field and Customer Success Account Managment (CSAM) leadership and a broad network of contacts focused on solving capacity-related challenges. This two-way exchange of information enables us to develop an early deal pipeline and more effectively plan resource-specific capacity that shapes our cloud data center growth strategy for each region.
We’re now seeking to hire a talented program manager based in the Puget Sound, to support the Americas. Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Work closely with cross organizational teams, including analysis of the opportunity pipeline to develop leading indicators that predict business opportunities and expansion challenges with accuracy. Act as a capacity ‘Account Manager’ for all regional capacity opportunities and challenges.
Become a trusted advisor to regional leadership teams for infrastructure planning, execution, and resolution of capacity-related issues.

Bachelor's Degree AND 2+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience.

title: Analytics Manager, Global Affairs
description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Global Affairs team works to ensure that artificial intelligence benefits people, communities, and countries around the world. We engage with policymakers, institutions, and stakeholders to help shape the policies and partnerships that enable AI to expand economic opportunity, accelerate innovation, and deliver broad public benefits.

A critical part of this work is understanding how people are using AI and translating those insights into credible, evidence-based analysis that can inform public policy, strengthen public understanding, and demonstrate the real-world applications of AI.

About the Role

We are seeking an Analytics Manager to help Global Affairs develop and communicate data-driven insights into how people and businesses are using ChatGPT, with a particular focus on local and regional trends across the United States and other priority markets.

In this role, you will analyze privacy-protective, aggregated usage data to identify meaningful patterns in AI adoption and use. You'll explore how people are using AI to work, learn, create, build businesses, and solve everyday problems, translating complex datasets into accessible insights that support policy development, strategic communications, stakeholder engagement, and public education.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical skills with an instinct for what makes data meaningful to policymakers, journalists, business leaders, and the public. You should be comfortable working with large datasets, identifying compelling patterns, evaluating the limitations of available evidence, and collaborating with policy and communications colleagues to turn findings into clear, credible narratives.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys moving between quantitative analysis, strategic problem-solving, and storytelling. You'll have the opportunity to help build a new analytical capability within Global Affairs and shape how OpenAI understands and communicates the adoption and use of AI across different communities.

This role is based in San Francisco, Washington, DC, or an approved remote location. Work arrangements and relocation eligibility will depend on the approved location.

In this role, you will:

Develop Local and Regional Insights

 - Analyze approved, aggregated ChatGPT usage data to identify geographic patterns in AI adoption and use, including trends across states, metropolitan areas, and other markets where the data supports reliable analysis.

 - Develop insights into how people are using AI for education, workforce development, entrepreneurship, small business activities, professional productivity, and other areas of economic and social opportunity.

 - Identify regional differences in adoption, use cases, and engagement that can inform Global Affairs' policy priorities and stakeholder outreach.

 - Develop market-level profiles and recurring analyses that illustrate how AI is being used across different communities.

 - Identify emerging trends and noteworthy patterns that can support engagement with policymakers, civic leaders, institutions, and the media.

 - Evaluate the representativeness, limitations, and appropriate interpretation of available data to ensure findings are accurate and responsibly communicated.

Support Policy and Communications Strategies

 - Partner with Global Affairs policy, communications, and partnerships teams to translate analytical findings into compelling, evidence-based narratives.

 - Develop state- and market-specific insights to support policy initiatives, public affairs campaigns, legislative engagement, and regional communications.

 - Identify data-driven stories that illustrate how people and businesses are using AI, including applications related to economic opportunity, education, productivity, and everyday problem-solving.

 - Support the development of reports, fact sheets, presentations, data visualizations, talking points, and other materials for internal and external audiences.

 - Translate complex findings into clear, accessible explanations while accurately communicating uncertainty, methodological limitations, and the distinction between observed usage and broader societal outcomes.

 - Respond to time-sensitive analytical requests related to policy developments, communications opportunities, and stakeholder engagement.

Build Scalable Analytics Capabilities

 - Create dashboards, reporting tools, and repeatable analytical processes that enable Global Affairs teams to access relevant geographic and thematic insights.

 - Collaborate with internal data science, research, product, and engineering teams to identify useful datasets, improve analytical methods, and develop new approaches to understanding AI adoption and use.

 - Establish consistent metrics and methodologies for tracking trends over time and comparing geographic markets.

 - Develop analytical frameworks that connect usage patterns to broader research questions about economic opportunity, workforce transformation, education, and AI access.

 - Combine internal insights with relevant public datasets, where appropriate, to provide additional economic, demographic, or geographic context.

 - Ensure all analysis and reporting follow OpenAI's privacy, security, and data governance requirements, including appropriate aggregation, approved data access, and safeguards against identifying individual users.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 4+ years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, economic research, public policy analytics, or a related quantitative field.

 - Are proficient in SQL and experienced working with large, complex datasets.

 - Have experience using Python, R, or comparable analytical tools to conduct quantitative analysis.

 - Have experience developing dashboards, reports, and data visualizations using tools such as Tableau, Looker, or similar platforms.

 - Can independently structure analytical questions, identify relevant data, conduct rigorous analysis, and communicate findings clearly.

 - Have a strong instinct for identifying what is interesting, surprising, or consequential in a dataset—and why it matters to a particular audience.

 - Understand the importance of analytical rigor, including data quality, sampling limitations, representativeness, and the distinction between correlation and causation.

 - Can translate technical findings into concise, accessible insights for nontechnical stakeholders, including communications professionals, policymakers, and organizational leaders.

 - Enjoy collaborating across functions and translating analytical work into actionable recommendations.

 - Are comfortable managing competing priorities and delivering high-quality work in a fast-moving environment.

 - Bring intellectual curiosity about AI, public policy, economic opportunity, and how emerging technologies affect people and communities.

Nice to Have

 - Have experience using data to support public policy research, government affairs, strategic communications, or public-sector decision-making.

 - Have worked with geographically disaggregated data, including state-, county-, or metropolitan-level datasets.

 - Have experience combining proprietary datasets with public data from sources such as the U.S. Census Bureau, Bureau of Labor Statistics, or Bureau of Economic Analysis.

title: Applied Scientist, Product Policy
description:
About the Team

The Product Policy research team studies how people use and experience AI, generating evidence to inform product, policy, and safety decisions. We partner with researchers, data scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams to understand AI’s effects on people’s lives, including well-being, youth experiences, and social and emotional use.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Applied Scientist to help design, execute, and analyze large-scale longitudinal research on AI use and well-being. You’ll work closely with research leads to translate scientific questions into rigorous studies, combining survey responses with behavioral data to understand how people’s experiences with AI evolve over time.

This is a hands-on role spanning applied analysis, research methods, and study execution. You’ll build reproducible analytical workflows, assess data quality and representativeness, and help establish reliable infrastructure for ongoing panel research. Your work will support research involving teens and adults, including studies of AI companionship, and help turn findings into useful evidence for product, policy, and safety partners.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with research leads to develop study designs, survey measures, and analysis plans for longitudinal research on AI use and well-being.

 - Conduct statistical analyses of survey and behavioral data, including evaluating selection and response bias, account-linkage patterns, and sample representativeness.

 - Prepare and validate analysis-ready datasets, implement analysis plans, and produce clear summaries and visualizations using reproducible workflows.

 - Develop quality checks across survey programming, fieldwork, data delivery, and repeated study waves to identify inconsistencies and improve research reliability.

 - Own day-to-day study execution, coordinating timelines, vendors, and cross-functional dependencies to deliver high-quality research on schedule.

 - Collaborate with data engineering and privacy partners on responsible account linkage, data flows, logging, and retention.

 - Support human-subjects research review, including Institutional Review Board (IRB) documentation, protocol amendments, and consent and assent processes.

 - Maintain clear documentation of methods, measures, assumptions, and protocol changes, and contribute analysis and methodological materials for research readouts, publications, and peer review.

 - Communicate findings, limitations, and practical recommendations to technical and nontechnical partners, and build reusable tools and processes that improve future studies.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience conducting applied quantitative research in social science, behavioral science, human-computer interaction, statistics, or a related field.

 - Bring strong foundations in survey research and statistical analysis, with experience working on panel studies, longitudinal datasets, or human-subjects research.

 - Are comfortable using SQL and Python or R to prepare data, implement analyses, validate results, and create visualizations.

 - Understand how recruitment, missing data, participant attrition, and measurement choices can affect the interpretation and generalizability of findings.

 - Can move between analytical work and practical execution, managing multiple timelines and collaborators while maintaining scientific rigor.

 - Communicate clearly, lead with the key takeaway, and connect methodological choices and findings to the decisions they inform.

 - Exercise sound judgment when working with sensitive data and research involving minors.

 - Enjoy building structure in ambiguous environments and collaborating across disciplines.

Nice to Have

 - Experience combining survey responses with behavioral or product data.

 - Familiarity with preregistration, measure validation, reproducible research, and academic publication or peer-review processes.

 - Experience working with research vendors, survey platforms, or IRB and ethics-review partners.

 - Research experience related to AI-human interaction, digital well-being, youth development, or social and emotional uses of technology.

title: Compute Electrical Engineer, Robotics
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an Electrical Engineer to develop the AI inference compute systems that power OpenAI’s humanoid robots. This role combines compute architecture, high-speed digital design, onboard power electronics, and compact HDI PCB development.

We’re looking for a self-driven engineer who takes ownership from concept through deployment. Above all, you should enjoy hands-on engineering: bringing up boards, characterizing interfaces, and tracking challenging failures to their root cause.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own compute hardware architecture and development, from component selection and schematic design through PCB layout, validation, and deployment.

 - Design and integrate high-speed interfaces—including PCIe, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, USB, and DisplayPort—balancing bandwidth, connectivity, power, and signal integrity.

 - Develop onboard DC-to-DC conversion and power distribution to meet efficiency, transient-response, sequencing, and power-integrity requirements.

 - Define HDI PCB stackups, dielectric materials, via structures, and routing strategies that balance electrical performance, manufacturability, reliability, and cost.

 - Lead bench bring-up and validation, including test planning, high-speed interface characterization, power measurements, and debugging through verified resolution.

 - Partner with thermal, mechanical, EMC, and software teams to integrate compute hardware into tightly constrained robotic systems.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 5+ years of experience developing compute hardware or similarly complex high-speed electronics, with demonstrated ownership of complete designs.

 - Bring strong hands-on measurement and debugging skills, including practical experience with oscilloscopes, probing techniques, and interface validation.

 - Understand high-speed digital interfaces deeply enough to make architectural tradeoffs and diagnose issues across hardware and software boundaries.

 - Have strong signal-integrity and power-integrity fundamentals, a solid foundation in power electronics, and practical experience designing complex HDI PCBs.

 - Can use a Linux shell, write simple shell scripts, connect over SSH, and perform basic Ethernet and network troubleshooting.

 - Take initiative, turn ambiguous requirements into concrete engineering plans, and follow through to deliver working systems.


ADDITIONAL, PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience designing around AI inference SoCs or accelerators, including their power, memory, and communication architectures.

 - Familiarity with how AI inference workloads map to silicon capabilities, including compute throughput (TOPS), DRAM bandwidth and capacity, and how workload requirements and DRAM technology choices affect achievable performance and performance per watt.

title: Electrical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an Electrical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working test stations, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from architecture and circuit design through validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will develop electrical test systems for board bring-up, programming, functional test, and characterization, partnering with mechanical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to carry validated stations from prototypes into repeat builds.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own PCBA test-station architecture, including device-under-test interfaces, programmable power, electronic loads, signal routing, instrumentation, and protection.

 - Translate board requirements and likely failure modes into test coverage, measurement methods, and pass/fail criteria. Partner with board designers on design for test, test-point access, programming interfaces, and diagnostics.

 - Design and bring up fixture interface boards, switching circuits, harnesses, and connectors. Release schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and interface definitions.

 - Integrate oscilloscopes, meters, power supplies, loads, and data acquisition hardware; validate calibration, timing, accuracy, and repeatability across stations and board revisions.

 - Develop and debug programming and communications interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, and Ethernet as required by the board. Diagnose power, signal-integrity, grounding, and contact problems.

 - Design and validate current limiting, power sequencing, ESD protection, interlocks, and fault recovery appropriate to the hardware under test.

 - Partner with mechanical engineers on probe access, connector mating, board support, cooling, and serviceability. Work with firmware and software partners to define interfaces and integrate test stations with shared software.

 - Write, debug, and maintain test code for instrument control, board programming, automated sequences, diagnostics, and result logging. Collaborate with software partners on reusable frameworks, code reviews, and reliable releases.

 - Establish station commissioning, calibration, maintenance, and configuration control. Track board identity and revision, firmware version, test limits, and station configuration with each result.

 - Use reference boards, independent measurements, and deliberate fault checks to distinguish board failures from fixture or software errors. Improve test coverage, false-failure rate, cycle time, and station uptime.

 - Own test-station deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including station correlation, build support, operator training, and troubleshooting. Release configurations and documentation that keep lab and factory results consistent.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong intuition for analog and digital circuits, power delivery, electronics debugging, and reliable measurement.

 - Move comfortably from architecture and circuit design to soldering, probing, scripting, and troubleshooting in the lab.

 - Care about grounding, shielding, contact quality, calibration, and evidence that a test detects the faults it is intended to find.

 - Take ownership from prototype through reliable daily operation, balancing rapid iteration with clear documentation and maintainable test systems.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant electronics test-system projects from ambiguous requirements through working hardware, validation, and sustained use.

 - Hands-on capability in circuit and fixture-interface design, schematic interpretation, board bring-up, power delivery, signal switching, and instrument integration.

 - Ability to independently debug PCBAs and test hardware using oscilloscopes, meters, logic analyzers, and systematic root-cause investigation.

 - Ability to write, debug, and maintain code that interfaces with real hardware in Python or a comparable language, including instrument control, sequencing, error handling, and structured result logging.

 - Practical understanding of grounding, signal integrity, calibration, measurement uncertainty, ESD controls, power sequencing, and electrical protection.

 - Ability to release clear test and hardware documentation, coordinate across engineering disciplines, and support hands-on deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Prior PCBA functional-test or automated-test-equipment experience, including design for test, test coverage, fixture correlation, and new-product builds at contract manufacturers.

 - Experience with embedded programming, diagnostic firmware, and board interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, or Ethernet.

 - Experience with PCB design tools, shared test-automation frameworks, production data systems, or robotics hardware.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Commission a reusable PCBA test station with documented coverage, acceptance criteria, and traceable results; deploy and validate a reproducible configuration at a contract manufacturer.

 - Demonstrate measurement repeatability and intended fault detection using reference boards, independent measurements, and known-fault cases. Track false failures, cycle time, and uptime against agreed improvement targets.

 - Release hardware documentation, versioned test code, commissioning checks, and troubleshooting procedures that enable lab and contract-manufacturer teams to reproduce, operate, and maintain the station

description:

We are developing scalable forecasting infrastructure to help us understand and anticipate business dynamics in an increasingly complex, usage-based world. Our models are foundational to planning, pricing, operational efficiency, and growth strategy - supporting key investment decisions and unlocking OpenAI’s full potential.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for a senior Machine Learning Data Scientist to lead our forecasting initiatives. You’ll be one of the founding members of the Forecasting pillar within Strategic Finance Data Science, responsible for building and scaling robust, interpretable, and production-ready forecasting systems. Your models will power critical business decisions by predicting core metrics such as DAU/WAU, revenue, LTV, compute consumption, and profitability.

You’ll collaborate with product managers, researchers, engineers, and finance leaders to operationalize forecasting insights, influence company-wide strategy, and build foundational forecasting capabilities at OpenAI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Build statistical and machine learning models to solve forecasting needs across product, finance, infrastructure, and GTM domains.

 - Experience building or scaling forecasting platforms in a high-growth company.

title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer, Search - Knowledge Graphs
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information.




ABOUT THE ROLE

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information. In close partnership with researchers, we bring modeling advances into production and improve how AI systems discover, retrieve, and use knowledge.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Researcher to lead Search Integrity: the systems that distinguish useful web content from spam, manipulation, and other adversarial or low-quality material.

The challenge extends beyond evaluating individual pages. A page may appear credible in isolation, while its links, metadata, or relationships with other sites reveal coordinated manipulation. As AI makes convincing content easier to produce at scale, detection systems must adapt to increasingly sophisticated adversaries.

You’ll define the technical approach, build classifiers and evaluations, and shape how integrity signals influence what Search indexes and retrieves. Working closely with Search and broader Safety and Integrity teams, you’ll use frontier models to advance detection methods and bring them into production.

 - Define the technical direction for Search Integrity, identifying gaps and determining which problems and interventions to prioritize.

 - Develop AI and ML systems to detect spam, scams, phishing, malicious domains, prompt injections, and other adversarial or low-quality web content.

 - Discover useful signals across page content, links, domains, metadata, and relationships between websites, including patterns that reveal coordinated manipulation.

 - Build evaluations that measure detection quality and how integrity interventions affect the information Search surfaces.

 - Translate detection signals into indexing, ranking, and filtering decisions, improving what models can retrieve and rely on.

 - Serve as the technical owner for integrity within Search, partnering with researchers, engineers, and broader Safety and Integrity teams to build and deploy these systems.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - Deep experience in web spam, search quality, adversarial content detection, or related integrity problems at scale.

 - Strong applied ML and research skills, with experience developing classifiers, detection methods, and evaluations for real-world systems.

 - An understanding of how adversaries manipulate content and links, coordinate across sites, and adapt to detection systems.

 - A track record of independently defining ambiguous technical problems and driving solutions from experimentation through production.

title: Software Engineer II - Growth
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Software Engineer II, Growth
We are seeking a Software Engineer II for the Growth Marketing Engineering Team. You are the kind of engineer who gravitates toward the hardest problems at the intersection of technology and performance marketing: designing a low-latency bidding optimization engine, building a reliable creative generation pipeline, or defining the architectural patterns that will shape how Quince scales its growth stack. You operate with high autonomy, hold yourself to exceptional standards, and naturally raise the bar for the engineers around you through rigorous code reviews, sharp technical judgment, and a bias toward clean, durable solutions over quick fixes.
Responsibilities
Designing and implementing software features and components, following best practices and coding standards with minimal supervision.
Contributing to identifying the root cause of complex problems, scale, and stability challenges.
Proposing a solution to mitigate them in the short/medium/long term horizon.
Keeping up-to-date with new technologies, frameworks, and best practices in software development, and applying them to improve the performance and reliability of software systems.
Writing and maintaining technical documentation, API specifications, code documentation, and technical design documents.
Participating in code reviews and contributing to the development of coding standards and best practices.
Mentoring junior engineers and contributing to their professional growth and development.
Leading software development projects and working collaboratively with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality software products
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
At least 2 years of professional experience working in building user facing products.
Experience in advertisement performance tooling is a plus.
Proficient in using debugging tools and techniques.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Ability to work independently as well as part of a team.
Understand the hustle of a startup and are good with handling ambiguity.
Effectively communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Curious, quick learner, scrappy and someone who loves to experiment.
Pay Range: $188,000 - $203,000 + bonus + equity
WHY QUINCE?
Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

Role Summary The Director of Supplier Development, Industrialization & Quality will lead a team responsible for end-to-end supplier execution, capability building, tooling industrialization and quality assurance across Rivian's global supply base. Merging pre-PPAP development engineering with post-PPAP quality management, this role establishes a single point of accountability for parts and systems from concept and tooling kickoff through ramp-up and serial production. The ideal leader brings deep automotive or EV industrialization experience, combining technical rigor with a "boots on the ground" problem-solving methodology to ensure flawless program execution, capacity realization and zero-defect quality across launch and current production vehicles. Responsibilities Strategic Organization Leadership: Build, lead and mentor a high-performing global team of Supplier Development, Industrialization & Quality Engineers across major commodity sectors (e.g. Chassis, Battery, Drive Unit, Thermal, Interior, Exterior and Power Distribution). Cradle-to-Grave Part & Supplier Ownership: Oversee end-to-end component ownership, streamlining supplier communications and cross-functional alignment across both pre-PPAP development and post-PPAP production quality. Upstream Quality Prevention: Engage early in program development cycles alongside Engineering and Purchasing to conduct DFM, DFMEA and PFMEA reviews, resolving downstream ramp and quality constraints long before Start of Production (SOP). Tooling & Capacity Industrialization: Oversee supplier industrialization timelines, tool kickoffs, tooling audits and station-by-station capacity mapping (JPH / throughput modeling, sensor checks and Poka-Yoke validations) to resolve yield bottlenecks and secure confirmed production volumes. Rigorous PPAP & Launch Gatekeeping: Enforce strict APQP/PPAP gatekeeper discipline, executing Safe Launch containment protocols, Rate-at-Rate verifications and mandatory recovery glide paths for supplier milestones. Rapid Problem Solving & On-Site Triage: Deploy resources directly to supplier facilities during critical ramps to perform root-cause analyses (5-Why, 8D, PFMEA updates) and drive immediate yield and quality recovery. Supplier Performance & Governance: Establish and track global supplier scorecards, quality metrics, and audit schedules, driving corrective action plans and ongoing continuous improvement initiatives across the supply chain. Cross-Functional Executive Partnership: Collaborate closely with Procurement, Hardware Engineering, Manufacturing Operations and Program Management to escalate risks, present recovery models and align sourcing strategies. Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, or Manufacturing), Supply Chain Management or a related technical field. Master’s degree preferred. Cradle-to-Grave Domain Expertise: Proven track record of managing components through the entire lifecycle - from early engineering design reviews, APQP and PPAP approval to serial production quality management. Technical Mastery: Deep proficiency in core quality and manufacturing tools such as APQP, PPAP, PFMEA, SPC, 8D, 5-Why, Poke-Yoke systems and Lean Manufacturing. Perform mechanical inspection using torque wrenches, screwdrivers, and tape measures.

Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, blueprints, and manufacturing drawings.

Work closely with Engineering, Quality, and Production teams to meet customer and production requirements.

High School/GED diploma required.
Demonstrated knowledge of mechanical operations.

Knowledge and ability to use air impact tools and other hand-held tools.
2 years of mechanical assembly and/or electrical wiring experience. Candidates with electrical or mechanical trade school education may also be considered.
Preferred:
Previous experience in an assembly or manufacturing environment a plus.

Standing: All tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.
Lifting: Frequent lifting of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Walking: Occasional walking moderate distances (less than 1/8 mile).
Carrying: Frequent carrying of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 25 lbs.
Pushing: Occasional pushing of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
Pulling: Occasional pulling of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
Bending: Frequent bending and crouching to safely lift parts of various sizes and shapes.
Reaching: Continuous full range of motion from above the shoulders to below the knees.
Handling: Continuous handling of parts ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Other: Respirator certification required.

Typical sales will be $20k to $100k, and involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.

Analyze: Identify customer painpoints and areas of opportunity with an analytical mindset combined with a customer-centric lens.
Build: Build the digital CS playbooks, taking advantage of the programs and resources other teams have built, design agent architectures, write prompts, integrate with external systems (Salesforce, Samsara platform, Customer Success tools), build guardrails, and write clean Python code that the team can maintain.

title: Business Operations Generalist
description:
COMPANY BACKGROUND

Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.




THE ROLE

We are looking for a Business Operations Generalist to join Specter's lean BizOps team. This person will work across deal support, pricing, market strategy, planning, finance, and company systems. Today the work leans more commercial, including working with our GTM teams on sales materials, customer value cases, and proposals. In a given week, it can mean a customer business case one day and a CRM cleanup the next. Some of it is strategic. Some of it is unglamorous. Part of the job is building the templates and systems that make that work repeatable, so the role will likely look different in 6 months, and may be less GTM oriented then. We want someone who enjoys that variety, jumps into new problems as they come up, owns the outcome, and leaves each process better than they found it. The right person is analytical, commercially sharp, highly organized, and comfortable working with leadership, sales, finance, product, and engineering in the same day.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - You will put together pricing, proposals, customer business cases, and value models for complex deals, and support contract review. Over time, you will turn this work into templates and systems the sales team can run on their own.

 - You will build business cases for new markets and new products, and keep the team current on what competitors are doing.

 - You will help leadership and the sales team see the pipeline clearly through forecasting, CRM hygiene, and dashboards.

 - You will support planning, budgeting, and board and investor reporting, and track spend across the business, including production, R&D, SaaS, and vendor spend.

 - You will build processes, documentation, and decision frameworks where today there may only be spreadsheets, Slack threads, and ad hoc decisions.

 - You will handle the day-to-day work that keeps the business running: cleaning up data, coordinating vendors, chasing down numbers, and taking problems from "someone should figure this out" to a clear owner and outcome.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3 to 5 years of experience in consulting, investment banking, or investing, or in business operations, revenue operations, or a similarly analytical role at an early-stage, high-growth startup.

 - Strong with spreadsheets and financial models, and comfortable in a CRM.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills.

 - Good judgment and the ability to prioritize when everything feels urgent.

 - A low-ego team player who takes on the detailed, behind-the-scenes work without being asked and improves it over time.

 - A builder mentality: you are excited to create the first version of a system and turn one-off work into something others can reuse.

 - A generalist who enjoys variety and is excited to take on whatever problem matters most, knowing the role will change as the company grows.

 - Comfortable working without much direction or full context. You find what you need, make a reasonable call, and flag what you assumed.

 - You use AI tools to improve systems and get more done, without handing your thinking to them.

 - Interest in physical AI, hard industries, critical infrastructure, defense, energy, or industrial technology and the ability and desire to get up to speed on technical products.

 - Based in San Francisco and excited to work in person.

title: Engineering Manager, Sandboxes
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Testability has long been a priority for Stripe. Before users trust code with their money, they need to verify that it’s safe and correct. This need drove Stripe to build test mode and, more recently, Sandboxes, which enables safe, isolated, and scalable testing.
As businesses build with AI and agents, their testing needs are evolving. Stripe customers use claimable sandboxes to add Stripe capabilities to prototypes before business registration. Once onboarded, they provision isolated test environments to support agents’ exploration. These capabilities help developers and agents build and test their integrations with Stripe.
The Sandboxes team defines, builds, and operates these testing capabilities. We work across Stripe to make our products testable, helping businesses develop with confidence and shaping the future of Stripe’s developer platform.
What you’ll do
You’ll lead and grow the Sandboxes engineering team, setting technical direction and operating critical systems. You’ll build a culture of operational excellence and thoughtful product development.
You’ll work directly with users to understand their needs and partner with Product, Design, and Data Science to shape and deliver the team’s strategy. The role combines building reusable testing capabilities across Stripe with attention to the details that make developer tools effective and easy to use.
Responsibilities
Lead engineering planning and execution, partnering with Design to build clear, useful testing experiences.
Shape the team’s strategy and roadmap, aligning partners across Product, Design, Infrastructure, Marketing, and Operations.
Own delivery from problem definition through rollout and ongoing operation, improving both system performance and the user experience.
Uphold high engineering standards across the team’s codebases and development practices.
Partner with Recruiting to hire engineers and build a diverse, high-performing team.
Coach and mentor engineers, provide candid feedback, and support career development tailored to their goals.
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, we encourage you to apply.
Minimum requirements
4+ years of engineering management experience, directly managing and growing teams of 5+ engineers building and shipping products at scale.
8+ years of full-time software development experience.
Experience building reusable, extensible software that supports a range of user needs, with strong user empathy and a commitment to high-quality user experiences.
Strong problem-solving skills, with a track record of finding practical solutions to complex challenges.
Experience turning ambiguous goals into clear priorities and delivering multiple high-impact workstreams.
A track record of building a supportive environment with candid feedback and high expectations.
Technical depth to guide architecture and product design discussions and help engineers make informed tradeoffs.
Experience taking ownership of initiatives and moving work forward independently.
Preferred qualifications
Strong product and design judgment, including the ability to simplify complex user experiences.
Experience making decisions and building strong working relationships across teams.
Experience building and leading a distributed team across multiple locations and time zones.
Experience building developer tools or platform capabilities.
Experience building testing tools or capabilities that help users test within a product.
Experience building AI agent systems or tools that support agent-driven development.

title: Head of Product Sales, Payouts
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Stripe is investing in building out its Payouts product sales team to help prospects and customers move money globally with greater speed, flexibility, and control. Our growing footprint of Payouts products (Instant, Next day, Global payouts, FX, MCS solutions) enable businesses to send funds to sellers, service providers, contractors, creators, claimants, customers, and other third-party recipients around the world.
You will represent Stripe across our global markets externally while helping develop and strengthen our culture internally. You know what it takes to build and scale a business structurally and methodically. You have a strong understanding of technical and financial concepts and enjoy working closely with Product and Engineering teams, as well as broader Sales and go-to-market organizations.
As the Head of Product Sales, Payouts, you will be a critical member of the go-to-market leadership team. You will drive the strategy and execution of Stripe’s Payouts GTM, accelerating adoption and revenue growth across Payouts, platform and marketplace payout capabilities, cross-border payouts, FX/MCS solutions, payout methods, and recipient experiences.
What you’ll do
Own and drive the global go-to-market strategy for Payouts.
Recruit, inspire, and lead a high-performing global team responsible for delivering ambitious adoption and revenue targets across Stripe’s Payouts portfolio.
Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, Product Marketing, Finance, and other cross-functional teams to align the Payouts GTM strategy and product roadmap with customer needs.
Establish Stripe as a strategic partner to businesses seeking to modernize how they move money to customers, sellers, service providers, and other recipients.
Operate effectively at the highest levels of a matrixed organization, bringing together multiple functions to deliver against shared customer and revenue goals.
Serve as the voice of the customer, translating market feedback into actionable insights that inform product strategy, prioritization, and execution.
Scale Payouts business to fastest growing part of Money Management
Responsibilities
We are looking for a seasoned leaderwith a proven track record of building teams, delivering outstanding results, and maintaining a long-term, user-first mindset. This leader will thrive amid ambiguity, operate effectively in a high-growth environment, and bring structure to complex problems. Ideal candidates will have deep sales management and leadership experience, domain experience in payments, solid product knowledge, including bringing new products to market, developing go-to-market strategies, scaling technology sales teams, and building trusted relationships with senior customers and internal stakeholders.
Recruit, develop, and lead a global team focused on the Payouts business across AMER, EMEA, APAC.
Coach the team in developing consultative, solution-oriented sales skills across every stage of the sales cycle.
Create structure and focus for new GTM ideas, use cases, and product sales campaigns. Drive execution, measure results, and make timely recommendations based on performance.
Manage day-to-day operations, with a focus on performance against key adoption, pipeline, and revenue metrics.
Drive revenue growth, increase product adoption and attach rates, and acquire new users.
Partner with regional and account sales leaders to embed Payouts into Stripe’s broader customer strategy.
Engage directly in the largest and most strategic opportunities, developing executive relationships and helping the team win and grow complex customers.
Develop a deep understanding of customers’ funds flows, operational requirements, and regulatory considerations, and translate those needs into compelling Stripe solutions.
Lead with clarity and context, developing a compelling plan aligned with Stripe’s overall direction.
Build repeatable sales motions that address the needs of platforms, marketplaces, enterprises, fintechs, and other businesses moving money to third parties.
Continuously improve programs and operating mechanisms by introducing new ideas, sharing best practices, and strengthening Stripe’s customer engagement model.
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. Preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
15+ years of technology sales experience.
10+ years of people leadership experience.
5+ years of experience in payments, financial services, or money movement.
Demonstrated experience building and scaling global teams that consistently deliver against ambitious goals.
Experience bringing new products to market and building repeatable go-to-market motions.
A builder’s mindset, with the ability to drive immediate results while establishing the foundations for long-term growth.
Deep understanding of payments, payouts, treasury, or financial infrastructure and the complex funds flows that support global businesses.
Excellent relationship-building skills, with experience engaging senior executives and customers at all levels.
Ability to explain complex technical, operational, and financial concepts in clear, accessible language.
Strong cross-functional leadership skills and experience influencing Product, Engineering, Marketing, Finance, and regional Sales organizations.
Highly analytical, with a deep understanding of how to use data to guide decisions and improve the performance of revenue teams.
Detail-oriented and willing to help a growing team navigate the operational aspects of scaling a global business.
Ability to think globally, act regionally, and thrive in a multicultural, fast-moving environment.
Experience representing an organization publicly and communicating effectively with customers, partners, regulators, the press, and internal employees.
High energy, a strong work ethic, disciplined execution skills, and a willingness to do what it takes to deliver results.
A true team player who puts Stripe and its users first.

title: Product Designer, Risk
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Product Design team defines and delivers user-facing experiences across Stripe. Product Designers work closely with engineers, product managers, researchers, strategists, operations, data scientists, and marketers to shape products from early strategy through launch and iteration. You’ll be joining the Risk team, which shapes how businesses get started on Stripe, build trust, stay compliant, and grow with confidence. The work spans businesses of every size and helps keep both our users and Stripe’s ecosystem safe. Risk is a high-impact design space where the problems are both strategic and complex. As a designer on the team, you’ll help bring clarity to critical user moments, reduce friction for legitimate businesses, and raise the craft bar where trust, ease, and confidence matter most. This role is a strong fit for a designer who is energized by complexity, motivated by impact, and excited to turn difficult systems into simple, intuitive experiences.
What you’ll do
In this role, you’ll design experiences that help businesses start and grow successfully on Stripe. You’ll work closely with cross-functional partners to define problems, shape direction, and ship high-quality experiences.
Responsibilities
Translate complex systems, policies, and operational constraints into clear, thoughtful product experiences
Identify high-leverage opportunities that improve coherence across journeys, touchpoints, and surfaces

description:
The Core Data Science team builds the products and data assets that let teams across Zoox measure and improve the autonomy and operational performance of our fleet. In this role, you'll focus on fleet simulation — the environment our data teams use to develop, test, and evaluate the algorithms that orchestrate our autonomous fleet (dispatch, routing, and vehicle assignment) and to understand how those algorithms perform before they reach the road.   You’ll piece together the constituent components into a coherent, easy-to-use simulation environment, filling in the gaps, and building generalizable mechanisms so data scientists can measure their algorithm's impact on fleet efficiency. You'll join a diverse, experienced team with rapidly growing scope while working with one of the industry's most valuable autonomous vehicle datasets. In this role, you will:
  • Design, prototype, and help deploy algorithms for vehicle assignment, staging, routing, and pricing
  • Model the inputs to orchestration (rider demand, data-collection value, servicing needs, events, and policies) as objectives and constraints
  • Work with specialists in marketplace economics, forecasting, and autonomy to turn their models into decisions the fleet acts on
  • Measure impact on revenue, utilization, and rider experience through simulation, offline evaluation, and online experiments
  • Contribute to how we evaluate and roll out orchestration improvements
Qualifications
  • PhD or MS with 2+ years of relevant industry or research experience, in operations research, robotics, controls, transportation, computer science, applied math, or a related field
  • Deep expertise in at least one of: combinatorial/integer optimization, stochastic optimization or control, reinforcement learning/approximate DP, network flows, or marketplace/demand modeling, plus the curiosity to work across the rest
  • Strong coding skills in Python, C++, or Rust; you write clean, tested, version-controlled code
  • Ability to turn ambiguous real-world problems into well-defined models and explain the tradeoffs to non-specialists
  • Good communication and collaboration skills
Bonus Qualifications
  • Internship or research experience in ride-hailing, delivery, logistics, or AV fleets (dispatch, routing, rebalancing, pricing)
  • Algorithms deployed in production or used on real operational data
  • Publications in operations research, transportation, or robotics venues
